name: run-finished-interrupt-outcome-accepted
description: an interrupt outcome on RUN_FINISHED is described 1.0 material, not something to strip or reject: it survives enforcement without a warning, and it closes the run rather than failing it
kill: drop RunFinishedInterruptOutcomeSchema from the RunFinishedOutcomeSchema union — enforcement then strips the outcome and warns "Removed unrecognised material at '/outcome' on RUN_FINISHED", which fails `noWarnings` (verified). Making the RUN_FINISHED case in verifyEvents treat an interrupt outcome as a failure kills the `completed` expectation, and swallowing RUN_FINISHED rather than delivering it kills `eventTypes`. WHAT THIS FIXTURE DELIBERATELY DOES NOT CLAIM: the TypeScript client also copies the interrupt onto `agent.pendingInterrupts`, and nothing here can see that — the format has no key for it, and it is read only by the NEXT runAgent() call, which a single-run replay never makes. This fixture used to be called `run-finished-outcome-interrupt-populates-pending` and named that assignment in its description; deleting the assignment left it green. It is renamed to what it actually proves. Covering the pending-interrupt bookkeeping belongs to the agent's own lifecycle unit tests.

interrupts.message: Approve the transfer before the run continues.

dotnet.intentional: The .NET client's event surface is ChatResponseUpdate.RawRepresentation, and the builder-only events yield no update: TEXT_MESSAGE_START and TEXT_MESSAGE_END open and close the message being assembled and hand a consumer nothing, so they cannot appear in a delivered list however faithfully the client processes them. The list here is the base list minus exactly those; every event this fixture is actually about is still in it, in order. RUN_FINISHED carrying the interrupt outcome is still delivered rather than swallowed, which is the half of this fixture the list is here to pin.
